spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶1:** At the time when the Divine Human was sent forth into spiritual combat clothed in the first encompassing truth of [GAP-1] ardent divine love, which He imparted to the primal state of the will that exists [GAP-2] within that single encompassing truth — [GAP-3] He laid bare and captured the proprium, the very intention of spiritual death, [GAP-4] and all its subordinate faculties of evil.

**¶2:** When the Divine Human ascended out of the deepest hell, [GAP-5] the Divine Truth proceeding from Good brought forth the ruling falsities that He had captured [GAP-6] as constituent states, those [GAP-7] of [GAP-8] the realm of falsity from evil, so that from them this spiritual world might be constructed and all things ordered according to the Divine design. From that time onward, the reservoirs in which evils and falsities had been stored [GAP-9] — He destroyed and laid waste the [GAP-10] and all that had been contained within them.

**¶3:** Just as a stagnant mingling of truth and falsity, from which the natural affections and the thoughts are captured and drawn out by the net of discernment, and only the residual corrupted truths and the lowest natural perceptions rooted in that state remain behind — so it is with the reservoirs of spiritual death. The [GAP-11] Divine Human captured their deliberate intentions of evil and the derivative evils that were [GAP-12] contained within them, and the reservoirs were left behind in their own proper state.

**¶4:** Thus the condition of the realm of falsity from evil is such, and so too the reservoirs that existed within it.

**¶5:** Just as the organized form of a person's life contains many particular faculties within it, so [GAP-13] the realm of falsity from evil contains [GAP-14] reservoirs of evil from its very origin — [GAP-15] all [GAP-16] the particular faculties that depend from the one supreme ruling love of self, which is the [GAP-17] governing principle of the whole organized evil. A single origin is the origin of them all, because they all depend from that supreme ruling self-love which presides over the whole form. Should any particular faculty be severed from the extremity of [th]ese lesser ruling evils, the supreme ruling love that presides over them [al]l remains in its place just as it is — [GAP-18] and one finds that the organized evil still lives. Al[l] these subordinate ruling evils are firmly rooted within it. [GAP-19]

**¶6:** Wh[en] they shall sever from them [GAP-20] all of them, these lesser [GAP-21] ruling evils shall [GAP-22] become as states devoid of all spiritual life, because they might perceive [GAP-23] that they are firmly established [GAP-24] within the organized form of evil, with which they have been conjoined. [GAP-25]

**¶7:** In precisely this manner, the reservoirs of falsity from evil are the same — the sources from which [GAP-26] falsity from evil poured forth into existence.

---

*Note on method:* The "marsh" image (¶3) is among the most precise correspondences in this passage — stagnant water being truth that does not flow from its Divine source, mingled with the natural growths (reeds, plants) of the unregenerate external mind. The "body with many heads" image (¶5–6) corresponds to the Swedenborgian teaching that all particular evils are organized under a single ruling love of self, as members under a head, and that removing subordinate evils does not destroy the ruling love until that ruling love itself is overturned.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: At the time when the First Man was sent to the war in the first garment of [living fire], which he gave to the first nature that exists [...] in that single garment. [By it] he hunted Matter, the thought of death, [its rulers] and all its other powers.

When the First Man came up from the abyss, [...] the Living Spirit brought the rulers whom he had hunted [from every] element, that [substance] of [the land of] darkness, that he might construct from them this universe and fashion everything appropriate for the greatness. From that time on, the place of the storehouses of the elements [was left behind, and] he destroyed and laid waste the [land and] all that were in it.

Just like a marsh, of which the fish and birds are snared in a net, and only the waters are left behind and the reeds and the plants that grow in it, this is also the case with the storehouses of death. The [First] Man snared their counsels and [their k]in that were [in them], and the storehouses were left behind in their [dwelli]ng place.
So then, the case of the land of darkness is like this, as is that of the storehouses that were in it.

Just as the body of man has many limbs in it, [the land of darkness] has [storehouses from] its beginning [like] all [the limbs] that hang from the great head of the [body]. A single root is the root of them all, because they all hang from the great head that is on top of the body. Should a limb be cut from the tip of [the]se small [h]eads, the great head that is on top of them [al]l stays in its place the way that it is [and still] you find this person alive. Al[l] these sm[all h]eads are firmly set in it [...]

Wh[en] they will cut from them [the limbs of] all of them, these little [heads] shall [become] the corpses, because they might see [that they] be firmly set [...] in the body, which they joined wi[th it ...]
In exactly this way, it is also the case that the storehouses of darkness are the same, the things from which the [darkness gushed] forth.

fills.explanation: In Manichaean cosmology, "living fire" is one of the five light elements forming the First Man's armor; it corresponds perfectly to ardent divine love (fire = love in Swedenborg), and "living" distinguishes divine love from natural fire.
The garment of living fire was the means by which the First Man captured the powers of darkness; "By it" provides the instrumental transition from the giving of the garment to the hunting of Matter.

The list escalates from Matter itself to its subordinate entities; "its rulers" (archons) is the standard Kephalaia term for the next tier of dark powers, and ¶2 confirms "rulers" as the specific category hunted and brought forth by the Living Spirit.

The Living Spirit captured the ruling archons from every element of the dark realm; "from every element" specifies the comprehensive scope of the capture, matching the spiritual reading's "constituent states."

The element is identified as "that substance of the land of darkness" — the dark elements constitute the very substance of the dark realm, which the spiritual reading renders as "constituent states of the realm of falsity from evil."
"The land of darkness" is the standard Kephalaia formula for the realm of evil, corresponding to the spiritual reading's "realm of falsity from evil."

This directly parallels ¶3's conclusion that "the storehouses were left behind in their dwelling place" — the storehouse-place remained as an empty structure after its contents were removed, and then the land itself was destroyed.

"He destroyed and laid waste the land and all that were in it" is a stock formula in ancient cosmological texts, and "the land" refers back to "the land of darkness" which is the subject of the chapter.

"The First Man" is the standard Manichaean title for the divine emissary who descends into battle; it corresponds to the Divine Human in the spiritual reading and is used consistently throughout this chapter.
"In them" specifies that the kin of the dark counsels were contained within the storehouses, matching the spiritual reading's "contained within them."

"The land of darkness" is the consistent Kephalaia term for the dark realm, parallel to "the body of man" in the analogy's other half, and corresponds to the spiritual reading's "realm of falsity from evil."

"Storehouses" is the Kephalaia's consistent term for the reservoirs of darkness, and "from its beginning" establishes their primordial origin, matching the spiritual reading's "reservoirs of evil from its very origin."
The passage is an extended analogy comparing the storehouses to bodily limbs; "like" introduces the comparison — "storehouses from its beginning, like all the limbs that hang from the great head."
"The limbs" continues the body-analogy vocabulary established in the sentence's first half ("the body of man has many limbs"), corresponding to the spiritual reading's "particular faculties."
"The great head of the body" is the natural-plane image for the ruling love presiding over the organized form of evil; "body" completes the anatomical metaphor that governs ¶5–6.

The passage teaches that removing a subordinate limb does not kill the organism; "and still" expresses the persistence of life despite the cutting, matching the spiritual reading's "and one finds that the organized evil still lives."

In the body analogy, "limbs" are the particular faculties depending from the heads; severing "the limbs of all of them" strips every subordinate ruling evil of its operative faculties, making them into corpses — forms devoid of spiritual life.
"Little heads" has been the consistent term throughout ¶5–6 for the subordinate ruling evils dependent on the great head; the spiritual reading confirms these are "ruling evils."

When severed from the body, the little heads "become the corpses" — they transform into states devoid of spiritual life, matching the spiritual reading's "become as states devoid of all spiritual life."

"That they" provides the grammatical connection between "see" and "be firmly set," yielding "they might see that they be firmly set" — matching the spiritual reading's "they might perceive that they are firmly established."
"Darkness gushed forth" describes the emanation of falsity from evil from its source reservoirs, corresponding precisely to the spiritual reading's "falsity from evil poured forth into existence."
